long_biography.plain_text:
Carlo Perrone took charge of his family's publishing company at 24 after his father's death. As president and publisher of SEP, he steered Il Secolo XIX through colour printing, radio and a multimedia newsroom. Purchases of outside and family-held shares ultimately gave him control of the Genoa-based company.

The inherited regional newspaper moved into broader alliances under his leadership. SEP combined with La Stampa's publisher to form Italiana Editrice, and that business joined what became GEDI. Perrone served as GEDI vice chairman and led the European Newspaper Publishers' Association. ENPA named him honorary president, preserving a role in European publishing after his departure from GEDI's board.

uncertainties.detail: The authoritative 40.25-metre and 565-GT vessel is the 2017 Ocean King conversion Genesia. A registry-style page names Perrone Carlo as owner and manager, and Vallicelli's designer independently names owner Carlo Perrone. The captain's Italian-French, Italy-resident description matches the publisher's official profile. This should not be conflated with a distinct approximately 49-metre Feadship also called Genesia in public yacht databases.

Exact-name searches were performed on Forbes first and repeated with Il Secolo XIX, SEP, GEDI and Genesia anchors. No dedicated current Forbes profile for this Carlo Perrone was located; family members and same-name executives were not treated as substitutes.

Publishing is the clear wealth-creation sector and durable professional identity. However, Mercurio sold its GEDI stake to Exor and Perrone left the board in June 2024. ENPA's current honorary presidency is an industry role, not evidence of a dominant personal asset, so current primary industry remains Unknown rather than assuming sale proceeds are still media exposure.

The family newspaper platform predates Carlo by generations, and contemporary reporting says he took responsibility after his father's death. The dossier attributes only Carlo's documented share acquisitions, recapitalisation, operating decisions and mergers to him; it does not import other Perrone family members' industrial, publishing or investment facts.

GEDI and ENPA independently establish the 1956 birth year, while Prima Comunicazione gives Neuilly-sur-Seine. The full 7 June 1956 date appears in an original corporate-board declaration preserved on a third-party document host and is corroborated by Cinquantamila; the lower confidence reflects the declaration's non-canonical hosting.

GEDI appointed Perrone vice president in 2020, but its June 2024 release says he left the board when Exor acquired 100% of the group. The biographies therefore present the GEDI position as completed and use ENPA's current honorary presidency for present orientation.

ENPA's current exact-person biography is proposed as the Company Website profile. Focused searches did not verify a dedicated personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website above the identity threshold; organisation accounts and namesakes were excluded.
The biographies omit the yacht, point-in-time debt and share percentages, current net worth, private family detail and unrelated family history. No live or compiled change is authorised.
